utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-02-63-PT, the Prosecutor versus Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour. It's Antoinette Issa on behalf of the Prosecution and with me is Ms. Lada Soljan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you Ms. Issa. Have you become the lead Prosecutor on this case or where is Mr. Peter McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'm certainly not the lead counsel in this case. Mr. McCloskey is actually making another appearance simultaneously in another courtroom on a related matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It helps me understand the merits of your motion to join this case with others.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We hope so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jelena Nikolic, representing the accused, Mr. Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. This is a Status Conference in accordance with Rule 65 bis. The purpose of this Status Conference is that, first, to organise exchanges between the parties so to have aware preparation for the case. And the second is to provide the Defence with the opportunity, especially the accused, an opportunity to see the Judges, if he has some problem he may raise the issue in relation, including the mental and physical condition of the accused. Mr. Nikolic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. I hear and understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have anything to complain during your stay in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I have no complaints about the detention. The situation is normal, the personnel is behaving properly, so I have nothing to state in that regard. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not sure at this stage when will this case be on trial but it might be sometime at the beginning of next year. So there is still a long way to go. You have to take care of yourself. If there is any problem, please do not hesitate, through your counsel or directly, to inform us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Well, as for the preparation of this case, what's the situation now, Ms. Issa? Would you please brief me about the latest developments of this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, as Your Honour may know, we are still pretty much in the early stages of this case. This is I think the only the third appearance by Mr. Nikolic. We have disclosed quite a bit of material to counsel. We're -- this process is of course still ongoing, and we are of course awaiting the decision on the joinder application, and I believe that for the time being there are no issues other than one that counsel may raise in relation to the ongoing material in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Jelena Nikolic, do you have anything to mention at this time on this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. The problem with electronic disclosure or -- the electronic system of disclosure is quite suitable for data searches and this is something that is accessible to the Defence; however, the Defence would like to have all the documents that are relevant, factually and legally, to Mr. Nikolic. We would like to transfer that to our database so that we can create a CaseMap database. When all the documents are transferred to the database, it's not possible to conduct searches of the material any more. It means that the analysis of these documents is being made more difficult, unless I am directly connected to the IDS, or the -- the EDS, the electronic database search. So because of this, our -- we need more time to be able to work and to prepare the case. For example, a couple of days ago, the transcript from two other trials related to Srebrenica were disclosed to the Defence, the Krstic and Blagojevic Jokic cases. This is about 26.000 pages of transcripts. In order to analyse them properly and quickly, it's possible to do this only electronically. However, when this is transferred to the computer and when we start to work in our usual way, it's not possible to conduct searches and make our own database, which would be the foundation of creating a CaseMap database. We have similar problems regarding the translation of transcripts from other cases. The Prosecution is not in a position to translate them and they have sent us, at least those parts which are part of the supporting material in the audio version. They have sent us audios on DVDs so the Defence then only has the option of listening to this material, listening to the DVDs from other cases. And which are -- these transcripts are integral parts of the material that's being disclosed. I think that this would be what I have to say in brief, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, I'm a layman in the computer science. I know next to nothing about how to find a document, without the help of other technical assistants. However, Ms. Jelena, you only presented me a problem. You did not ask for any relief on this aspect. And Ms. Issa, would you please be some help to this issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll certainly try, Your Honour. I believe Mrs. Nikolic actually raised this issue this morning at the 65 ter conference and we advised her that we would look into it, at least preliminarily today, to see if we could find a solution to the problem that she has presented to us and essentially what we've -- my preliminary answer is we are still presently trying to find a solution to assist counsel. But just by way of an explanation, the electronic disclosure suite system is designed so that a search can only be done within the actual system itself. The programme that can highlight a particular word or name is only associated with the system itself so if one were to try and pull a document from the EDS system to another folder, that programme is obviously not -- no longer associated -- would not be associated with this other folder, and so she cannot do a second search. But she can certainly do a search on the EDS system itself. Now, one potential solution we are looking at which we still haven't had an opportunity to confirm is to potentially use the basket that is contained within the system, it is sort of like a folder that's within the EDS system, and it's called a basket. And what counsel can do is pull documents from within the larger EDS system and put it into the basket to save as their own file and then re-search within the basket itself. One can do a second search in that basket itself. That is one solution that we are potentially proposing. But having said that, we are still looking into the matter and we will try and find a solution as soon as possible. Having said all of that, of course, the -- you know, the old way was just to provide paper documents to counsel and then this is a far -- certainly an improvement on that in my respectful submission, and it doesn't preclude counsel from doing her searches within the system itself although if we can enhance their ability in some way, we will certainly attempt to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just need some clarifications. That so-called basket is called "Srebrenica basket" or "Nikolic basket" or whatever?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, it's just called an individual basket is the reference to it. It might be there might be a potential way of individualising it to -- for the different counsel. I'm not entirely sure about this at this stage because, again, this is simply a preliminary response that I was able to gather from -- through the computer support personnel. So there might be potentially a way of individualising it so that that basket or folder or whatever one might call it would be individualized to a particular counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And is it possible to install some software in the Defence's computer so that they could perform the same functions as you did?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I should just first of all mention that the -- I don't believe the Prosecution actually even is able to pull documents and search them outside of the system so we don't even have that capability. But whether or not we can -- software can be installed to perform that. To be honest at this stage, Your Honour, I'm simply not able to respond to that question but that's something that I'm perfectly happy to look into and determine and would certainly advise counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Another issue is about the audio and video disclosure. I wonder if there is any translations or transcripts for those materials, if you disclose to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well the transcripts are of course public and Defence just has access to those transcripts which are largely public. The material that we disclosed in the audio version is simply the B/C/S version of the testimony that took place in court. I don't believe -- my understanding is that it would be the responsibility of Registry to translate the transcripts in and of themselves. We thought it would be a good solution to provide counsel with the audio version in B/C/S as a way of assisting counsel in that way. But I don't believe at this point we are in a position to translate the transcripts, and I am not -- I don't believe it's certainly the responsibility of the -- the OTP. But the transcripts themselves are public and counsel does have access to those transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I wonder if there is any index so that the Defence when using it could see which transcript is corresponding to which audio tape or videotapes. Are there any index like this?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, as Your Honour can see, Ms. Stewart is not with me today. She chose to attend in the other matter with Mr. McCloskey and I would normally rely on her to get that response. However, I would certainly look into that. I think there might be an index. I can't say at this stage because Ms. Stewart did in fact disclose this material to counsel. Perhaps counsel might be able to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. I believe that it is a great improvement to have all the materials electronically disclosed. In other cases, it will a great help to the Defence for them to prepare their own case. Thank you. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I guess that's all for this Status Conference. And the next Status Conference will be held, according to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, at a later stage. I hope the special Bench will make a decision on the motion of joinder before that time. I believe that's all. The hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
